title: NORTH CLAY SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The North Clay School board met in regular session Wednesday night.

Assistant Principal/Athletic Director Rich Grubaugh gave board members a construction update and final preparations for the upcoming school year.  School Registration for North Clay began on July 19th and runs through Saturday for Online Registration.  In-person registration will be on Wednesday in the South Gym at North Clay Elem/Jr. High. Hours are 10am until noon and 1pm until 6pm.  New Teacher Orientation will be held on Friday, July 31st.

Superintendent Keith Price presented a summary of the proposed teacher contract.  The contract would be for three years with pay increases of 6% for 26-27, 6% for 27-28, and 5% for 28-29.  Other items in the contract included: an additional personal day per year, an additional sick day per year, an adjustment in the bereavement day language, a $40 increase of the monthly health insurance contribution for 26-27 and a $40 increase each year for the next two years of the contract, an increase in the amount tuition reimbursement and increasing the retirement incentive from 2 years to 4 years.  A complete copy of the contract will be posted on the school website soon.

Superintendent Keith Price discussed the increasing distraction that cell phones are having inside the classrooms and provided an update on the state’s anticipated new legislation that would require schools to restrict phone usage in classrooms.  The revised policy goes into effect starting this school year.

In personnel action the board accepted the letter of resignation of Nicole Boose as a paraprofessional, hired Kaitlyn Eade as a paraprofessional for the 2026-2027, accepted the letter of resignation of Devin Hilfirty as Sponsor of the Senior Class, approved unpaid leave request for Brenda Warner, and hired Bailey Burdine and Cameron Stone as permanent substitutes.

title: BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
The American Red Cross is facing an emergency blood shortage and needs donors to give now and take steps to protect patient care.  A steep decline in blood donations since the end of May has created a growing gap between supply and patient need.  Every donation is critical to rebuilding the nation’s blood supply.

There will be a Blood Drive at the Flora Oddfellows Lodge on Friday from 1 to 5 pm.  Donors at this drive will get a Fandango Movie Reward by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  You can make an appointment to donate at Red Cross Blood Drives by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  Save time with RapidPass. Complete your pre-donation reading and health history at RedCrossBlood.org/RapidPass or with the Blood Donor App before your appointment.

The next blood drive in our area will be on Tuesday, August 11th at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church from Noon to 6 pm.  Then on Thursday, August 13th there will be a blood drive at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.  People donating at these drives will get a $20 Amazon Gift Card by email.

title: NORTH WAYNE BOARD
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board met in regular session on Thursday.

Superintendent Adam Ellis told board members that School registration will be online August 3rd through 11th with in person registration on August 10th and 11th at the school the child will attend.  August 12th and 13th will be teachers institute days and the first student attendance will be August 14th.  Mt. Erie will hold an open house on August 12th from 4:30 to 6 pm, at Johnsonville from 5 to 6: 30.  Cisne Middle and High School will have open house on August 19th from 5 to 6 pm.

The Board authorized Ellis to amend the FY 27 calendar as needed, approved Co-op agreement in girls high school basketball with Wayne City and Webber and approved the school improvement plan for SIP grant.

In personnel matters the board accepted the resignation of Sarah Scott and hired April Walker as an individual aide for the 2026-27 school year.

title: BACK TO SCHOOL VACCINE CLINICS
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is having a series of Back-to-School vaccine clinics.

The next clinic is Thursday from 8:30 am to 5 pm at the Health Department on 12th Street.  Appointments are not necessary but are appreciated.  Appointments can be made by calling 618-662-4406.

Illinois state law requires certain immunizations for children and adults enrolled in childcare, school, or college.  State law also mandates immunizations for adults in specific fields of work.

There will also be Back-to-School vaccine clinics on August 3rd, 6th, 12th, and 13th from 8:30 am to 6 pm.  The final clinic will be from Friday, August 14th from 8 am to Noon.

Again, appointments are not necessary, but appreciated, if you have questions call the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406.

title: NEW GEFF SUPERINTENDENT
full_story:
Geff Community School District 14 announced the hiring of their newest Superintendent and Principal, Dr. Patrick Rice.  Dr. Rice comes to Geff from his most recent role of Superintendent of Schools in Cairo, where he served for four years.  Dr. Rice officially took the reigns at Geff Grade School on Tuesday.

Dr. Rice is currently, and will remain a clinical professor at the University of Illinois, instructing superintendents and principals focusing on Education Policy and Organizational leadership.  In addition to the 10 years Dr. Rice served as the Director of Field Service and Equity Director for the Illinois Association of School Boards, Rice has served as principal at multiple schools, as needed for a total of eight years, has written four books, and has over 20 publications in journals of advanced learning.

title: OFFICE COORDINATOR NEEDED
full_story:
51st District State Senator Chapin Rose and 102nd District State Representative Adam Niemerg announced that the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) is looking to hire an office coordinator for Red Hills State Park in Lawrence County.

The job involves maintaining records and files for the park, explaining site rules, regulations and services that the park offers to the public, preparing documents and reports, creating and maintaining work schedules, preparing materials for various hunting, fishing, and recreational programs and other related tasks.

The deadline to apply is Tuesday, July 21st.  More details are available, including a complete job description, salary and benefit information, and instruction for applying by visiting the IDNR website online.

title: FCC 3 on 3 TOURNAMENT
full_story:
Frontier Community College will continue celebrating its 50th anniversary with a 3-on-3 Basketball Tournament on Saturday, August 15th, at 10 am.  The tournament will be held in the Student Services Parking Lot on FCC’s campus.

The event will feature three age divisions: junior high for students in sixth through eighth grade, high school for students in ninth through 12th grade, and an adult division for participants 18 and older.

Teams may include up to four players and will compete in a double-elimination tournament format.  The team fee is $60.

The tournament is part of Frontier Community College’s ongoing 50th anniversary celebration and provides an opportunity for students, alumni, families, and community members to enjoy a fun day of basketball and Bobcat spirit.

For more information or to register a team, contact Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: LETTUCE RECALL
full_story:
Taylor Farms has expanded its voluntary recall of iceberg lettuce products sourced from central Mexico due to a potential link to the multistate Cyclospora outbreak that has sickened people across the US.

Products with the potential to be contaminated with the diarrhea-causing parasite were shipped to 27 states, including Illinois, Texas, Florida, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey, the California-based company said in a statement Friday.

“We are actively removing the implicated products,” the statement said, adding that the company has stopped sourcing lettuce from an implicated lot in central Mexico.  Earlier this week, US health officials identified lettuce from a supplier in Mexico as a source of cyclospora contamination in food served at Taco Bell restaurants in five Midwestern states.

The Taylor Farms recall announcement listed 25 shredded lettuce and salad mix products sold under eight different brand codes.  Taylor Farms did not respond to an emailed request for the full names of those brands or retailers.  The recalled products were shipped as recently as Thursday and have “best by” dates as late as August 3rd.

Sysco, the nation’s largest food distributor, has halted distribution of all Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce products sourced from Mexico and instructed customers to destroy them.

Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that infects food that has come into contact with human feces, most commonly when produce is irrigated or washed with contaminated water.  When ingested, the parasite causes intestinal illness marked by “frequent and sometimes explosive bowel movements,” according to the CDC.

In 2026, cyclospora has sickened at least 1,645 people in the US and hospitalized 141, according to the CDC, which is investigating more than 5,000 additional illnesses that may be linked to the parasite.  This time last year, only 249 cases had been reported.

The CDC initially warned consumers to avoid eating shredded lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia.

“Taco Bell worked swiftly to voluntarily remove the product from restaurants and the affected ingredient has been removed from our supply chain nationwide,” the company said in a statement Friday.
